To prevent starvation in operating systems, techniques such as priority scheduling algorithms (like Rate Monotonic Scheduling or Earliest Deadline First Scheduling), Round Robin Scheduling, and resource preemption are utilized. These methods ensure that all processes receive a fair share of system resources by allocating time slices (time quanta) for each process and interrupting (preempting) a process if it exceeds its allocated time slice, thus preventing any single process from monopolizing resources and causing starvation.
